_help: Regions and their dig sites. stars = stars needed to open the region. layers = rock bands from the surface down (weight = how thick). bedrock = the unbreakable rock at the bottom. inclusions = hard lumps mixed into a layer. gadget = the new tool you get here (see tools.json). Each site: creature = a creature id, or "bonebed" for a mixed site that favours bones you're missing. slack = how much spare energy (1.3 tight .. 1.8 relaxed). map = where the pinned note sits on the expedition map (0-100).

regions.name: Desert Badlands
regions.blurb: Layer-cake cliffs of sand and sandstone, baked by the sun. A perfect place to start.

sites.name: Horned Hollow
sites.note: A farmer spotted a horn sticking out of a gully. Start here!

sites.name: Quick Claw Gully
sites.note: Tiny, light bones. Brush gently!

sites.name: Plate Mesa
sites.note: Something with big flat plates is buried up on the mesa.

sites.name: Badlands Bonebed
sites.note: A jumble of bones from all over the badlands. Fill the gaps in your collection.

regions.name: Sea Cliffs
regions.blurb: White chalk cliffs above a pebbly beach. Ancient sea reptiles and flyers rest in the chalk.

sites.name: Gull Point
sites.note: Long, thin, hollow bones. Something that flew!

sites.name: Anning's Ledge
sites.note: Paddle-shaped bones in the blue clay.

sites.name: Saucer Cove
sites.note: Someone found a ring of eye bones as big as a plate.

sites.name: Chalk Bonebed
sites.note: A storm washed out part of the cliff. Bones everywhere!

regions.name: Jungle Riverbed
regions.blurb: A slow brown river cuts through mud and gravel under the trees. Watch for tangled roots.

sites.name: Sail Bend
sites.note: Tall back spines poking out of a mud bank.

sites.name: Giant's Ford
sites.note: The neck bones here are enormous.

sites.name: Trumpet Pool
sites.note: A curved, hollow crest was seen in the shallows.

sites.name: Riverbed Bonebed
sites.note: The river piled bones up on this bend for millions of years.

regions.name: Frozen Tundra
regions.blurb: Snow on top, ice and permafrost below. Polar dinosaurs lived here when it was a little warmer.

sites.name: Crest Ridge
sites.note: A fan-shaped crest frozen in the ice.

sites.name: Long Night Camp
sites.note: Huge eye sockets and a very long tail.

sites.name: Lump Hill
sites.note: A skull with a big bony lump on the nose.

sites.name: Permafrost Bonebed
sites.note: The thaw has opened a crack full of old bones.

regions.name: Volcano Ridge
regions.blurb: Old (and very asleep) volcanoes buried these bones in ash. Basalt is tough: plan your route.

sites.name: King's Crater
sites.note: Teeth as long as a ruler!

sites.name: Dome Rock
sites.note: A very thick, round skull in the ash.

sites.name: Armour Slope
sites.note: Bony armour plates and a tail club.

sites.name: Ashfall Bonebed
sites.note: One big ashfall buried a whole herd's worth of bones.
